newsitem.title: USA: Plane with 63 people aboard skids at NYC airport.
newsitem.headline: Plane with 63 people aboard skids at NYC airport.

text.p: A Delta McDonnell Douglas MD-80 jet skidded off the runway at New York's La Guardia airport on Saturday as it was landing but all aboard were safely evacuated, officials said.

The plane, designated as Flight 554, had 58 passengers and a crew of five. It was coming in from Atlanta when it skidded to the edge of the runway on touchdown, stopping short of Flushing Bay, an airport spokesman said.
The spokesman later told reporters the plane's front landing gear collapsed as the plane hit the ground and caused the craft to skid to the edge of the runway.
"The plane is not in the water. It is at the end of the runway and it is not on fire. The plane was foamed down as a precaution," the spokesman said.
Four minor injuries were later reported, all incurred while the passengers were being evacuated. One passenger was admitted to an area hospital.
The spokesman said the airport would be closed until noon EDT (1600 GMT) on Sunday.
La Guardia, in the New York City borough of Queens, was closed after the accident and other flights were rerouted to nearby John F Kennedy International Airport.
A USAir Fokker F-28 crashed on takeoff from La Guardia on March 22, 1992, and plunged into Flushing Bay, killing 27 of 51 passengers and crew.
Evidence suggested that accident, which occurred during a snowstorm, had been caused by a buildup of ice on the plane's wings.
